title: Normalized proper/open calculus on strict pro-etale towers
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring and, for every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use the constant ring sheaf $\underline B_T$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B_T))$, with strict inverse systems and module sheaves as in [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal T_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. These tower categories are the module categories on the diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. For a scheme map $u$ let $G_u=u^{-1}$ act termwise, with the canonical constant-ring identifications, and let $R_u^{\mathcal T}$ be total right derived termwise direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. Use $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$ with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$, and the exact open extension $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied termwise. Mates and composition adjunctions have the normalization of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting].
For a cartesian open square $(j:V\hookrightarrow T,j':V'\hookrightarrow T',g:T'\to T,g_V:V'\to V)$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], there is a canonical isomorphism on these derived tower categories
$$\beta_{j,g}:G_gj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!G_{g_V}.$$
Its inverse is the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ transpose of the open-extension unit $G_{g_V}M\to G_{g_V}j^{-1}j_!M\cong j'^{-1}G_gj_!M$. It is natural, equals the identity for identity base changes, and its successive-base-change composite equals the comparison for the composite, with the canonical pullback compositors. It also commutes with composition of open immersions. Evaluation on a finite constant coefficient object is the comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. These assertions hold for arbitrary $B$, including infinite $B$.
Consider a commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc} V&\xrightarrow{k}&W\\
r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\
S&\xrightarrow{i}&T\end{array}$$
with $p,r$ proper and $k,i$ quasi-compact open [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No cartesian hypothesis and no chosen factorization of the square are imposed. Put $W_S=W\times_TS$ with projections $b:W_S\to W$ and $q:W_S\to S$, and let $s=(k,r):V\to W_S$ be the induced map [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $s$ is a clopen immersion: it is open and closed, $bs=k$ and $qs=r$; thus $W_S=s(V)\amalg(W_S\setminus s(V))$ is a decomposition into open subschemes. Here clopen means an open immersion which is also a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^{-1}F$ for the natural projection which is identity on $s(V)$ and zero on its complementary open component. It acts termwise on strict towers and complexes. Define
$$\alpha_Q:G_pi_!\xrightarrow{\beta_{i,p}}b_!G_q\xrightarrow{b_!\pi_sG_q}b_!s_!s^{-1}G_q\cong k_!G_r.$$
In a cartesian square $s$ is the identity and $\alpha_Q=\beta_{i,p}$. In a refinement square $V=S$, $r=1_S$, it is projection onto the clopen section $(k,1_S)$. For every commutative proper/open square above, define the normalized proper/open comparison to be the proper-adjunction mate
$$\gamma_Q=(R_p^{\mathcal T}k_!\varepsilon_r)\circ(R_p^{\mathcal T}\alpha_QR_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\eta_pi_!R_r^{\mathcal T}):i_!R_r^{\mathcal T}\longrightarrow R_p^{\mathcal T}k_!.$$
All these are transformations in the derived categories of strict towers. Write $\nu_V:V_{\mathrm{proet}}\to V_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For $M\in D(\mathcal T_V)$, suppose each $\operatorname{ev}_n M$ is the restriction of scalars, along a ring homomorphism $B\to\Lambda_n$ with $\Lambda_n$ finite commutative, of $\nu_V^*L_n$ for some $L_n\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Then $\gamma_{Q,M}$ is an isomorphism. Under the canonical direct-image and open etale/pro-etale comparisons [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], its $n$-th evaluation is precisely the normalized finite proper/open comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], including its refinement normalization. No uniform lower bound in $n$ is required.
The following identities hold as actual derived strict-tower transformations, for these squares and their horizontal or vertical pastings, with the canonical direct-image, pullback and open-extension composition identifications. For a pasted square use the mate of the pasted $\alpha$ with the composition adjunctions. For vertically stacked squares $Q_1,Q_2$ with left proper maps $r_1,r_2$, right proper maps $p_1,p_2$ and middle open $i_1$,
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\gamma_{Q_2}R_{r_1}^{\mathcal T}).$$
For horizontally adjacent squares $Q_1,Q_2$ with top opens $k,l$, bottom opens $i,j$ and proper verticals $r,p,q$,
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(\gamma_{Q_2}k_!)\circ(j_!\gamma_{Q_1}).$$
For a base change $b:T_1\to T$, with projections $a:W_1\to W$, $c:S_1\to S$, $d:V_1\to V$ and induced square $Q_1$, let $E_p^{\mathcal T},E_r^{\mathcal T}$ be the mates of the pullback squares. Then
$$(R_{p_1}^{\mathcal T}\beta_k)\circ(E_p^{\mathcal T}k_!)\circ(G_b\gamma_Q)=(\gamma_{Q_1}G_d)\circ(i_{1!}E_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\beta_iR_r^{\mathcal T}).$$
The comparisons for pasted squares use the intrinsic clopen-projection construction just specified; their alpha maps agree with the pasted alpha maps, with the canonical inverse-image and open-extension composition identifications. Thus the two displayed composition laws apply to every commutative proper/open square, including squares between intermediate open schemes in refinements of compatible composition towers, without a cartesian or identity-left hypothesis. The comparisons are independent of parenthesization. Squares with identity vertical maps give the identity on open extension, and squares with identity horizontal maps give the identity on derived direct image. All these equalities hold before evaluation; the evaluation functors are not assumed faithful.

The source states the etale result; the tower realization, finite-evaluation normalization and pro-etale extension are additional assertions to be proved, not quotations from the source.

proof.text:
The constant-ring identifications are valid for arbitrary $B$. By sheafification, maps from $\underline B_T$ to a ring sheaf $F$ are ring maps $B\to F(T)$: a map from the constant presheaf is determined by its section on the final object. The ring-sheaf adjunction therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(u^{-1}\underline B_V,F)=\operatorname{Hom}(\underline B_V,u_*F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(B,F(U))=\operatorname{Hom}(\underline B_U,F).$$
Here $(u_*F)(V)=F(U)$ because $U\times_VV=U$. Thus the canonical constant-section map is invertible, by the representing-object uniqueness argument: the two universal maps have identity composites since they represent the identity on these Hom sets. The identifications respect composition and ring maps because they send every constant section to itself. This checks the coefficients of the operations in [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], without imposing finiteness on $B$.

proof.text: With the coefficient identification of step 1 the module pullback is the exact inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Extension along an open is the localized-site functor of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], by weakly-etale localization. Apply these additive functors termwise to towers. Kernels and cokernels of towers are levelwise, so their exactness persists; the componentwise units and counits commute with transitions and give the termwise adjunctions. The diagram-site realization is a small ringed site, so its module complexes admit K-injective resolutions. The right adjoint of an exact additive functor preserves K-injectives. Consequently termwise direct image has its unbounded total derived functor; the termwise adjunction on homotopy categories and the canonical derived-adjunction theorem give $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Exact open extension and open restriction descend directly, giving $j_!\dashv G_j$ with their termwise units and counits. These are the operations and normalized adjunctions of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension].

proof.text: For the cartesian open square, localization gives $j^{-1}g_*\cong(g_V)_*j'^{-1}$, with the identity comparison on the same sections over the pulled-back test object. Hence $G_gj_!$ and $j'_!G_{g_V}$ are left adjoints of canonically identified right adjoints. The unit-normalized uniqueness of left adjoints supplies their canonical isomorphism $\beta$. Its inverse $t:j'_!G_{g_V}\to G_gj_!$ has $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ transpose equal to $G_{g_V}\eta_j$, followed by $G_{g_V}G_j\cong G_{j'}G_g$: this follows by composing the two adjunction Hom bijections and inserting the open unit. It is the inverse direction specified in the statement. The identities $j^{-1}j_!\cong1$ used here follow directly on the localized extension presheaf: for an object over the open there is exactly one lift to that open. These comparisons, units and their equations act termwise on towers and complexes, and descend by exact-functor factorization and the localization universal property.

proof.text: For successive base changes, transpose both inverse comparisons under the final open adjunction. Both transposes are $G_{hg,V}\eta_j$ followed by the same iterated inverse-image compositor; naturality of the unit identifies the successive transpose with this one. For successive opens transpose under the composite open adjunction: the unit is $G_{j_1}\eta_{j_2}j_{1!}\circ\eta_{j_1}$, so again the two transposes coincide. For an identity base change the transpose is the open unit, so the comparison is identity under the open-unit identification. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijections proves the base-change, open-composition and identity laws, with the canonical compositors, before any evaluation. At finite $B$ this is the canonical extension-by-zero base change of the existing node, since its restriction comparison and open unit are the same ones. In the Lean identity case, first check the two unit equations of moduleRComp on sections using Over.pullbackComp_id_left and Over.pullbackComp_id_right. Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso transfers them to module pullback. Evaluate the whiskered tower comparisons at each index, and use the naturality and unit laws of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso to obtain the derived pullback unit equations. Transposition under the open adjunction then proves beta_id and the analogous identity-open beta equation. The Lean beta_comp proof uses the general inverse-image square pasting identity of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-pullback-square-pasting]. A proved abstract adjunction lemma transposes the inverse beta composites: unit naturality, square naturality, and the defining betaInv unit equations reduce them to this identity. Cancelling the invertible beta maps recovers the stated forward comparison equality.

proof.text: Construct $s$ by the fibre-product universal property. Base change of the open $i$ makes $b:W_S\to W$ an open immersion. The commutativity $pk=ir$ says that $k(V)$ lies in this open. Restricting an open immersion to an open containing its image is again the same isomorphism onto its image: identify $W_S$ with $p^{-1}(i(S))\subset W$, and $V$ with $k(V)$ therein; the induced map is $s$, by the fibre-product uniqueness. Thus $s$ is an open immersion, with $bs=k$ and $qs=r$. The map $q$ is separated, being the base change of the separated map $p$. Since $r$ is proper, the proper-over-separated theorem, applied over $S$ to $qs=r$, makes $s$ proper. A proper immersion is a closed immersion. Therefore $s(V)$ and its complement $C$ are disjoint open subschemes covering $W_S$. This argument applies equally to the empty open and does not assume that $r$ is an identity or that the original square is cartesian.

proof.text: For a module sheaf $F$ on $W_S$, every pro-etale test object $H$ is covered by the two disjoint opens $H\times_{W_S}s(V)$ and $H\times_{W_S}C$. The sheaf axiom identifies its sections with the product of the two component section modules, since the intersection is empty. Projection to the first factor, extended by zero on the second, consequently defines a unique natural module map $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^{-1}F$. On a clopen immersion extension by zero and direct image agree by exactly this product formula (the other component is the zero module); thus this is the claimed projection and it commutes with restrictions, module maps, tower transitions and differentials. Compose it with the $\beta$ of steps 3-4 and the open-composition comparison to obtain exactly the displayed $\alpha_Q$. If the square is cartesian then $s=1$, so $\pi_s=1$ and $\alpha_Q=\beta_{i,p}$. If $r=1$ and $V=S$, then $s=(k,1)$ is the indicated clopen section and the projection is its component projection. This is a construction, not an inference from the finite-coefficient theorem. The direct-image adjunction unit is restriction to this component; the canonical map $s_!	o s_*$ is identity on it and zero on its complement. Consequently this sectionwise projection agrees with the adjunction definition in [def-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-arrows]. For the formal proof of pi_components, the adjoint triple J_s ⊣ G_s ⊣ R_s identifies G_s(pi_s) with the open-adjunction unit. For disjoint opens, restriction of a direct image from the other open is zero: each pulled-back test scheme is empty and the empty covering gives a zero section module. The ringed-open comparison identifies this restriction with actual module inverse image. The open adjunction then makes extension from the other open zero after restriction. This zero-object statement passes termwise to towers and through exact derived localization, so the complementary restriction of pi_s has zero target. This proof does not use faithfulness of evaluation.

proof.text:
Write $J_j=j_!$, suppressing the canonical compositors of steps 3-4. For vertically stacked squares, the alpha identity is
$$\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(\alpha_{Q_1}G_{r_2})\circ(G_{p_1}\alpha_{Q_2}).$$
After the beta identifications, the source is extension from the inverse image of the bottom-left open in the top-right scheme. The first component projection retains the inverse image of the middle-left open; the second retains the top-left open, which lies inside it by commutativity. Subdivide each test object by the two clopen decompositions of step 5. On the retained intersection both maps are the same canonical pullback identification; on every other intersection the composite and the outer projection are zero. The sheaf uniqueness axiom proves the identity. This is multiplication of nested identity/zero component projections, using the beta coherences already proved in step 4.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose); explicit projection calculation for the underived pro-etale alpha

proof.text:
For horizontally adjacent squares, with top opens $k,l$, bottom opens $i,j$ and proper verticals $r,p,q$, the identity is
$$\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(J_l\alpha_{Q_1})\circ(\alpha_{Q_2}J_i).$$
The first projection retains $l(W)$ inside the source-support open, while the second retains $lk(V)$ inside it. On their common retained component both sides give the same inverse-image identification; on its complement both sides are zero. Use the intersections of the clopen covers as in step 7 and glue. Extension by zero across the surrounding opens does not alter this calculation: on those opens it is the given map, and off them it is the zero map, by step 6. The beta/open compositors coincide by step 4. Hence the identity concerns the specified transformations, including their normalizations.

Base change sends the disjoint-open decomposition $W_S=s(V)\amalg C$ to $W_{1,S_1}=s_1(V_1)\amalg C_1$, by the fibre-product universal property. Its exact additive inverse image preserves the split product of module sheaves, so it preserves the identity and zero component projections. Steps 3-4 identify the surrounding open extensions. Writing $\theta:G_{p_1}G_b\cong G_aG_p$ for the canonical inverse-image square identification, these observations give
$$(\beta_kG_r)\circ(G_a\alpha_Q)\circ(\theta J_i)=(\alpha_{Q_1}G_c)\circ(G_{p_1}\beta_i).$$
Indeed, restrict both sides to each of the two pulled-back clopen components: on $s_1(V_1)$ both are the canonical composite pullback identification, and on $C_1$ both vanish. The pullback compositors identify $G_dG_r$ with $G_{r_1}G_c$; the sheaf uniqueness axiom gives the equation. No coefficient finiteness is used.

proof.text:
All functors occurring in $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are exact. Apply their sheaf transformations termwise to towers and then to complexes. Exact-functor factorization and the uniqueness part of localization descend their transformations and every equation of steps 3-4 and 6-9 to the unbounded derived strict-tower categories. Now take the mate of $\alpha_Q$ for $G_r\dashv R_r^{\mathcal T}$ and $G_p\dashv R_p^{\mathcal T}$. The mate definition is precisely
$$(R_p^{\mathcal T}J_k\varepsilon_r)\circ(R_p^{\mathcal T}\alpha_QR_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\eta_pJ_iR_r^{\mathcal T}).$$
This constructs the stated $\gamma_Q$, naturally on the derived tower category. Its transformation is fixed by this formula on that category. In particular it is not selected by asking for prescribed evaluations.

proof.text: Evaluation commutes with exact $G_u,J_j$ termwise. Choose a K-injective tower representative $I$ of an input. Its evaluation $I_n$ is K-injective by the tower-evaluation theorem, so $\operatorname{ev}_n(u_*I)=u_*I_n$ computes both $\operatorname{ev}_nR_u^{\mathcal T}$ and $Ru_*\operatorname{ev}_n$, with the canonical resolution comparison. These identifications preserve the adjunction units and counits: on homotopy categories the adjunction is the termwise one, and the canonical derived Hom bijection is computed by that adjunction into the K-injective representative. Evaluating that chain-map transpose gives exactly the transpose into $I_n$; the K-injective Hom bijection makes it the same derived transpose. Hence evaluating the mate formula of step 10 gives the single-level mate of the single-level clopen $\alpha_Q$. No assertion that evaluation is faithful is needed.

For a coefficient map $B\to\Lambda$, apply the ring-sheaf-change-adjunction theorem to $\underline B_T\to\underline\Lambda_T$. It supplies the canonical inverse-image and derived direct-image scalar-restriction comparisons and their adjunct identity. Open extension commutes with scalar restriction as well: its extension presheaf has exactly the same underlying additive sections and the restricted scalar action, and sheafification gives the same underlying sheaf with that action. The component projection also has the same identity/zero formula. Thus the adjunct identity and the mate formula identify the single-level $B$-mate on $\operatorname{Res}N$ with the restriction of the $\Lambda$-mate on $N$. This uses no flatness of $B\to\Lambda$ and does not assert that scalar restriction preserves K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition) and Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); scalar-adjunction compatibility from the cited ring-sheaf-change theorem

proof.text:
For finite $\Lambda$, first work on the etale site. The proper-support composition theorem gives a sheaf isomorphism $\delta:i_!r_*F\cong p_*k_!F$: both are the same subsheaf of $(ir)_*F=(pk)_*F$, and the comparison keeps the underlying section. It is the underived proper mate of the etale clopen alpha. To verify this equality, transpose under the open adjunction $i_!\dashv i^{-1}$. Localizing to $S$ identifies the right side with $q_*s_!F=r_*F$: extension and direct image along the clopen $s$ agree by the two-component formula of step 6. The transpose of $\delta$ is identity on these sections. The transpose of the proper mate also restricts to identity: its alpha retains the $s(V)$ component and the remaining inverse-image/direct-image unit-counit pair cancels by the adjunction triangle identity. Thus the two transposes, and hence the two sheaf maps, agree.
For $L\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ choose K-injective $J$ representing $L$ and a K-injective resolution $t:k_!J\to I$. Then $r_*J$ is K-injective, since $r^{-1}$ is exact. The derived proper mate transposes to the chain map
$$p^{-1}i_!r_*J\xrightarrow{\alpha}k_!r^{-1}r_*J\xrightarrow{k_!\varepsilon_r}k_!J\xrightarrow{t}I.$$
The canonical derived Hom bijection and the termwise adjunction identify its adjunct with $p_*t\circ\delta_J$. This is exactly the resolution normalization stated in [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. Its refinement normalization therefore agrees as well.

proof.text: The site-comparison hypotheses hold without a Noetherian assumption. Proper $p,r$ are quasi-compact by their finite-type hypothesis. Their diagonals are closed immersions; on an affine open a closed immersion is the spectrum of a quotient ring, hence its inverse image is affine and quasi-compact. Therefore $p,r$ are quasi-separated. These are precisely the qcqs hypotheses of the counit-normalized direct-image comparison. Exact etale open extension preserves the lower bound, since it preserves kernels, cokernels and zero objects and therefore cohomology; thus both $L$ and $k_!L$ lie in its required bounded-below domain.

source.place: Tag 099R (section-comparison), domain of etale/pro-etale direct-image comparison; qcqs checked from definitions

proof.text:
Apply the finite open comparison and the site pullback comparison to the etale alpha of step 13. They identify it with the pro-etale alpha: both keep the same clopen component, are identity there, and are zero on the complementary component. Exactness descends this equality from complexes. Let $A_T=\nu_T^*$ and let $b_u:A_TRu_{\mathrm{et},*}\to Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_U$ be the canonical comparison. Its specified counit equation is
$$\varepsilon^p_u\circ G_u(b_u)\circ a_u=A_U(\varepsilon^e_u).$$
Substitute this equation for $u=p,r$ in the proper-mate formula: naturality moves the open comparison past the units, and the two proper-adjunction triangle identities cancel the inserted unit-counit pairs. The remaining middle square is exactly the alpha square just verified. Equivalently this is the coefficient-square mate-pasting theorem, which assumes only those counit equations and that pull-comparison cube. Consequently the mate on $A_VL$ is, under the canonical source/target comparisons, $A_T$ applied to the normalized finite etale arrow of step 13. All the comparisons used are the specified ones: the direct-image comparison has the stated counit normalization, and open comparison is the adjoint comparison. The finite etale arrow and both direct-image site comparisons are isomorphisms by the cited theorems. Hence this pro-etale mate is invertible and has exactly the finite normalization asserted in the item.

proof.text: Let $M$ satisfy the stated witnesses, with a possibly different finite ring and lower bound for every $n$. Steps 11-12 transports evaluation of $\gamma_{Q,M}$ along the given isomorphism $\operatorname{ev}_nM\cong\operatorname{Res}\nu_V^*L_n$; steps 13-15 proves that transported arrow is an isomorphism. Evaluation is exact and tower cohomology is levelwise, so for every degree $a$ the morphism $H^a(\gamma_{Q,M})$ has isomorphic components at every $n$. A morphism of towers with isomorphic components is itself invertible: the component inverses commute with transitions by multiplying the original commutative transition squares by those inverses. Therefore each $H^a(\gamma_{Q,M})$ is an isomorphism, and the unbounded-derived cohomology criterion makes $\gamma_{Q,M}$ an isomorphism. This detects invertibility only. It does not infer equality of derived morphisms from equality of their evaluations, and it uses no uniform bound in $n$.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic); homology.tex Tag 02MZ (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian); component inverses written explicitly

proof.text:
Apply the two mate-pasting formulas to the alpha equations in steps 7-8, now in the derived tower categories of step 10. Pasting along the proper adjunctions sends $(\alpha_{Q_1}G_{r_2})(G_{p_1}\alpha_{Q_2})$ to
$$(R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\gamma_{Q_2}R_{r_1}^{\mathcal T}).$$
Pasting along the open functors sends $(J_l\alpha_{Q_1})(\alpha_{Q_2}J_i)$ to
$$(\gamma_{Q_2}J_k)\circ(J_j\gamma_{Q_1}).$$
These are the two displayed gamma laws. Use the composite-adjunction units and counits in the mate-pasting theorem. They correspond to the canonical proper direct-image compositor: right adjoints of the exact inverse images preserve K-injectives, so on a K-injective tower complex $I$ the composition is represented by the underived equality $(p_2p_1)_*I=p_{2,*}p_{1,*}I$; this is the normalization of the ringed-topos composition theorem on the diagram sites. The open compositor is similarly the unit-normalized left adjoint of iterated restriction from steps 3-4. For three proper maps, these underived identifications associate to the same triple direct image on $I$; for three opens the transposes are the same iterated restriction unit. The Hom/localization bijections and uniqueness of adjoints preserve these equations. Together with associativity of natural-transformation composition and the alpha projection identities, this proves independence of parenthesization. Identity horizontal maps give $\alpha=1_{G_p}$ and the identity clause of mate-pasting gives $1_{R_p^{\mathcal T}}$. Identity vertical maps give $\alpha=1_{J_i}$ and identity adjunctions give $1_{J_i}$. These are equalities of derived tower transformations on all inputs, before the finite-origin restriction. For the identity clauses, alpha_cartesian reduces the two identity squares to the beta identity equations from step 4. Abstract mate-pasting and conjugation with the identity adjunction transport these equations to the specified rId and jId normalizations.

source.place: Tags 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal); generic mate-pasting with the proved alpha identities

proof.text:
Finally take mates of the cube equation in step 9. The pullback square isomorphisms $G_{p_1}G_b\cong G_aG_p$ and $G_{r_1}G_c\cong G_dG_r$ have mates $E_p^{\mathcal T}$ and $E_r^{\mathcal T}$. The mate-pasting formulas, with the open beta transformations left untransposed, turn the left side of that cube into
$$(R_{p_1}^{\mathcal T}\beta_k)\circ(E_p^{\mathcal T}J_k)\circ(G_b\gamma_Q),$$
and the right side into
$$(\gamma_{Q_1}G_d)\circ(J_{i_1}E_r^{\mathcal T})\circ(\beta_iR_r^{\mathcal T}).$$
